compiled_state.description:
## Observation

The Lambda `bedrock-principal-audit` (us-east-1, description "Daily drift audit: Bedrock-capable IAM principals vs spend-cap enrollment", publishes to SNS topic `bedrock-spend-cap-alerts`) runs once a day at about 14:00 UTC (07:00 PDT) and emits a JSON report. Its `/aws/lambda/bedrock-principal-audit` log group over the last 60 days shows:

- 2026-09-13 04:17 UTC: first run, `drift: ["role/OrganizationAccountAccessRole"]`. 32 seconds later a second run reports `drift: []` with that role in `enrolled_roles`, so the role was enrolled at deploy time.
- 2026-09-13 through 2026-09-20: `drift: []` every day.
- 2026-09-21 14:00 UTC onward: `drift: ["role/OrganizationAccountAccessRole"]` on every daily run, 28 consecutive days through 2026-10-18, with no change in the report.
- 2026-09-24: one run also listed an IAM user with a `bakeoff-rebar-re…` prefix as drift; it did not recur.

The spend-cap Lambda `bedrock-spend-cap` (last modified 2026-09-25 16:03 UTC) carries the enrollment list in its `TARGET_ROLES` environment variable: 11 roles (`lmn-*`, `rebar-external-ci-bedrock`, `rebar-gerrit-instance-role`) plus `TARGET_GROUPS=Admin`. `OrganizationAccountAccessRole` is not in that list. The role has `AdministratorAccess` attached, so it is Bedrock-capable, which is exactly the condition the audit flags.

So the alarm is correct about the state and recurs because the state never changes: the role was de-enrolled (or the enrollment list was rebuilt without it) between the 2026-09-20 and 2026-09-21 runs, and no one has either re-enrolled it or taught the audit that it is an accepted exception.

## What is not yet established

- Whether dropping the role from `TARGET_ROLES` was deliberate. The spend-cap deny policy attaches to enrolled principals when the cap trips; enrolling the organisation access role would mean a tripped cap also denies Bedrock to the org-level admin path, which may be the reason it was removed. That decision is not recorded anywhere I could find (no ticket matches `principal audit`, `drift`, or `OrganizationAccountAccessRole`).
- Where the audit Lambda's source lives. `git grep enrolled_roles` across all local branches finds nothing, and `infra/` has no `principal-audit` reference, so the deployed code is not in this repository.
- Whether the SNS message is what the operator sees as "the recurring enrollment alarm", or whether a CloudWatch alarm sits on top (no CloudWatch alarm or metric filter references the audit log group).

## Verification (2026-10-24 04:55 PDT, read-only AWS, profile frontier, us-east-1)
- Lambda `bedrock-spend-cap` (LastModified 2026-09-25T16:03Z): 11 roles in `TARGET_ROLES`, `TARGET_GROUPS=Admin`; `role/OrganizationAccountAccessRole` is not enrolled.
- `bedrock-principal-audit` ran at 2026-10-24T14:00Z; the last 3 daily runs each report the same single drift entry, `role/OrganizationAccountAccessRole`.
- The `frontier` profile is the IAM user `joe_frontier`, not this role, so enrolling it does not change Bedrock access from this operator machine.
- `infra/terraform/bedrock_spend_cap.tf` sets the list in `variable "bedrock_cap_target_roles"` (default list) and passes it to the Lambda as `TARGET_ROLES` and to the Lambda's IAM permissions; the audit Lambda's own source is not in the repo.

## Decision (operator, 2026-10-24)
Enroll `OrganizationAccountAccessRole` in the spend cap, rather than exempting it. The role has `AdministratorAccess`, so it is Bedrock-capable, and while the cap is tripped it is the one Bedrock-capable principal the deny does not cover. When enrolled, the trip-time deny covers Bedrock invocation actions only; management and read calls stay allowed.

## Approach
1. Add `"OrganizationAccountAccessRole"` to the default of `bedrock_cap_target_roles` in `infra/terraform/bedrock_spend_cap.tf`, and extend that variable's description to name this role and what enrolling it means (the deny applies to it while the cap is tripped, for Bedrock invocation only).
2. Add a focused test that parses the Terraform default and asserts the role is enrolled, so a later edit cannot silently re-open the hole.
3. Landing the change does not alter AWS. Applying it is an operator step that updates the Lambda's `TARGET_ROLES` and its IAM permission list; it is performed only with the operator's go-ahead, and the plan output must show changes to this Lambda configuration and its IAM policy only.

## Scope
In scope: `infra/terraform/bedrock_spend_cap.tf` and one test. Out of scope: the audit Lambda's source (not in the repo), the cap threshold, and the other principals.

## Testing
```
pytest tests/infra/test_bedrock_spend_cap_handler.py -q
terraform fmt -check infra/terraform
make verify
```
Failure case: the new enrollment test fails on main because the default list lacks the role. After apply, `bedrock-principal-audit`'s next scheduled run (14:00 UTC) must report `drift: []`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] The Terraform default for `bedrock_cap_target_roles` includes `OrganizationAccountAccessRole` and its description says what that means (checked: new test, which fails on main).
- [x] `terraform fmt -check` and the existing spend-cap tests pass (checked: command output).
- [x] `make verify` is green on the Linux CI gate (`Verified +1` on the Gerrit change).
- [x] After the operator applies Terraform, the live `TARGET_ROLES` contains the role (checked: `aws lambda get-function-configuration`, recorded in a ticket comment).
- [ ] After the apply, the next scheduled audit run reports `drift: []` (checked: `/aws/lambda/bedrock-principal-audit` log line with its timestamp, recorded in a ticket comment).
